text:
Nashville arrives on a six-game winning streak, the latest a 4-2 win at Anaheim two days ago in which Roman Josi reached 800 career points. Vegas has won four straight, including a 5-3 home win over Utah, though the Golden Knights are playing without Noah Hanifin. The Golden Knights beat the Predators 5-2 on Oct 13, and Nashville has a chance to answer that tonight.

Our numbers favor Vegas, 3.28 expected goals to 2.78, which measures the quality of chances each side creates. At five on five, the Golden Knights have taken 52% of the expected goals in their games and Nashville 47%, and the Predators' streak is only half backed by the chances, with goaltending doing the rest. Vegas also has the better penalty kill. In net, Juuse Saros (projected) is at +9.2 goals saved above expected this season after finishing last season at -10.2. Adin Hill (projected) is at +1.8 after -15.0 last year.

Jack Eichel has a four-game point streak and a 76% chance to record a point, while Mitch Marner sits at 74%. Jesse Granger of The Athletic posted of Vegas's last game that "Marner drives into the slot, fakes a shot and dishes to Eichel, who one-times it top shelf." For Nashville, Steven Stamkos (34% to score) and Filip Forsberg (32%) lead the way, and Jonathan Marchessault could return from day-to-day status.
